{{Top|notoc=1}}
{{Quote|It was a very low-gravity environment. You could throw a lightsaber hilt a kilometer if you tried.|[[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], referring to [[The Home]]|<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Exile">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Planetary_gravity.png|thumb|right|250px|A planet's gravity was what pulled smaller bodies toward its center.]]
'''Gravity'''<ref name="Jedi Search">''[[Jedi Search]]''</ref> or '''gravitation'''<ref name="Rogue Planet">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref> was the attraction between two bodies, dependent on their masses and the distance between them. Empirically speaking, gravity was what kept a being's feet on the ground and caused dropped objects to fall. All bodies, including [[Planet/Legends|planets]], [[Moon/Legends|moons]] and [[Star/Legends|stars]], exerted gravity. The larger a body was, the more gravity it had, and the harder it "pulled" other things toward its center. On the surface of a planetary body, that direction was commonly referred to as "down." In [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]], however, there was very little natural gravity, which is why [[Starship/Legends|starships]] utilized [[Artificial gravity generator/Legends|artificial gravity generators]] to simulate it. [[Orbit/Legends|Orbiting]] a planet resulted from the perfect balance between gravity and the ship's forward motion toward the planet.<ref name="SWSA">''[[Star Wars Science Adventures: Emergency in Escape Pod Four]]''</ref>

In the modern galactic civilizations, there existed [[Antigrav/Legends|certain technologies]] that countered the effects of gravity. An example of common low-maintenance antigrav devices were the [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]], which allowed [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]] to hover, helped starships for liftoffs and landings. Other gravity-altering devices included [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] [[Tractor beam projector/Legends|projectors]] and [[Acceleration compensator/Legends|acceleration compensators]].<ref name="AOTC CS">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

Most inhabited planets and moons in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] had an acceleration of gravity at or near standard gravity of 9.81 [[Meter/Legends|m]]/[[Standard second|s]]². For beings who evolved on worlds that had standard gravity, traveling to planets that had lower or higher ones could be a disturbing experience. On a lower-than-standard gravity planet, a [[Human/Legends|Human]] could jump very high effortlessly. On a higher-gravity world, however, the same Human could feel plastered to the ground.<ref name="SWSA" /> For example, the planet [[Carida/Legends|Carida]] had a gravity nearly twice the galactic standard,<ref name="wizards">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030904carida1|series=Carida: Heavy Duty|text=Part 1: Weight Training}}</ref> which was turned into an advantage: Carida was the site of a reputed [[Carida Academy/Legends|Military Academy]], and its higher gravity enhanced the challenge of field maneuvers.<ref name="HNN52">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|news/13418_2.html|Carida Backs Military Creation Act}}</ref> Some believed that low-grav locations such as [[Columus/Legends|Columus]] had health benefits to obese beings by reducing strain on the [[Heart/Legends|heart]] and increasing mobility. It was not at all the case, however. In fact, those who maneuvered on a low-gravity planet reduced their muscle use, which only tended to slow metabolism.<ref name="HNN56">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|56|life/13516_1.html|Healthy Vacation Claims Disputed}}</ref>

Gravity was responsible for helping [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] find the missing planet of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], as all nearby objects were drawn towards the spot where Kamino was supposed to be, though nothing was recorded in the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]] at those coordinates.<ref name="AoC">{{Film|II}}</ref>
